_about: Wire frames of the upstream OpenClaw gateway at tag v2026.9.4 (github.com/openclaw/openclaw), taken from its unit tests and adapted for sessionKey/runId namespacing. Each scenario pins one interpretation contract documented in docs/UPSTREAM_INTERPRETATION.md. Source file:line is cited per scenario; those citations are recorded in bridge/protocol/openclaw/citations.json and checked by test/upstream-citations.test.ts, and the frames are replayed by test/upstream-frames.test.ts — do not edit shapes without re-checking the upstream tag. NOT EVERY FRAME IS COPIED. Three scenarios say COMPOSED in their own description: writer-claim-rebound-after-content, writer-claim-rebound-before-generation and writer-claim-rebound-after-start-zero-content. The 2026-09-12 adversarial review found composed parts in three more whose descriptions do not say so: aborted-user-stop-partial-text (the terminal frame is upstream's, the preceding delta is not), init-conflict-zero-content (the message is verbatim, the wire frame around it is ours) and compaction-explicit-stream-signals (both signals are anchored, the deltas between them are synthetic). On 2026-09-15 the citation check found that the errorMessage text of error-errorkind-rate-limit is ours as well (the upstream test pins only that it contains `Too many requests`). Three more are composed throughout and say so in their description: error-state-contention-dispatch, status-waiting-for-state-then-resume and aborted-then-save-warning-error (2026-10-03); agent-assistant-append-only composes its lifecycle end and final envelope around the two pinned frames. This list used to name four of seven while the fixture held nine scenarios: nothing read it.

aborted-user-stop-partial-text.description: src/gateway/chat-abort.test.ts:450-464 (v2026.9.5) — a killed run broadcasts state:aborted with a free-form stopReason ('user' is a caller value, NOT in any enum) and the partial text snapshot. The turn must finalize aborted on state alone; stopReason must never reclassify it.

aborted-tool-validation-errormessage.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:3707-3716 (v2026.9.5) — self-abort on tool-validation failure: state:aborted carries stopReason:'aborted' plus errorMessage. An aborted turn keeps its abort status; the errorMessage is diagnostic, never a persisted error.

payload.errorMessage: edit tool validation failed: edits: must be an array

error-timeout-stopreason-precedence.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:3776-3803 (v2026.9.5) — a timed-out abort (lifecycle end aborted:true stopReason:'timeout') is emitted as state:ERROR, not aborted: the gateway consumes stopReason BEFORE emitting. NEW at 2026.8.x: the payload also carries errorKind:'timeout' (the recorded classification must reach the browser) and NO `message` — the test asserts its absence.

error-errorkind-rate-limit.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:4505-4532 (v2026.9.5) — a 429 lifecycle error reaches the wire as state:error with errorKind:'rate_limit'. The upstream test asserts the payload has NO `message` and NO `errorDetail` (that field only appears when the runtime recorded a provider observation). The allowlisted wire errorKind survives as the message errorKind. The errorMessage TEXT of the frame is ours, not upstream's: the upstream test pins only that errorMessage contains `Too many requests` (the gateway renders the error with formatForLog), so only the errorKind and the absent message/errorDetail are upstream facts here.

payload.errorMessage: Provider call failed: 429 Too many requests

writer-claim-rebound-after-content.description: COMPOSED (not copied from one upstream test) — the 2026.8.1+ successor of the 7.1 embedded prompt-lock takeover, which no longer exists (attempt.session-lock.ts is gone since 2026.8.1; transcripts moved to SQLite). Parts, each cited: the message is thrown verbatim by src/config/sessions/transcript-write-context.ts:411 (SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError, identical 8.1->9.4); the error NAME is pinned by src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts:667; the wire rendering '<Name>: <message>' is pinned by src/gateway/ws-log.test.ts:130-132,139-140 (formatForLog), and server-chat.ts:1125 emits it as errorMessage on state:error. CONTRACT: unlike the 7.1 lock flavour, this one is NOT downgraded to complete — upstream's announce delivery retry loop may retry it (subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:136-171 isTransientAnnounceDeliveryError, used at subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:248: no retry on send evidence, then a typed retryability decides when present, then a permanent non-writer error refuses, and only then a writer rebound retries); a failed direct delivery is `ambiguous` on send evidence, otherwise `permanent_failure` for this rebound unless a typed retryability decides otherwise (subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts:612-623 via isPermanentAnnounceDeliveryError, defined at subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:173-179; the regex at subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:58-59 is only the shared definition; retry file byte-identical 9.2->9.4, direct-delivery classification unchanged in meaning). Atrium keeps the honest error card and classifies the turn session_write_conflict — its OWN class, NOT the retryable session_init_conflict: upstream throws the same text at commits after the model ran (tools may have had external effects) as well as before generation; here content has streamed, which proves the run generated, so Atrium's bounded auto-retry must not re-dispatch it (the pre-generation case is writer-claim-rebound-before-generation).

payload.errorMessage: SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence

writer-claim-rebound-before-generation.description: COMPOSED — the same rebound thrown while the attempt is still PREPARED: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-bootstrap.ts:286 (prepareInitialSessionWriter, reached from run/session-prompt-state.ts:54) and run/pre-persisted-user-turn.ts:101 (preparePersistedCurrentUserTurn, from run/attempt-session-prepare.ts:594), both before the agent loop emits agent_start (packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts:114) — which embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.ts:51-62 turns into {stream:'lifecycle', data:{phase:'start'}}. The prelude frames (chat state:'status', agent stream:'run_status') are the shapes captured on every run of a full 2026.9.4 bench run, which showed nothing else before lifecycle start; the terminal frame is as in writer-claim-rebound-after-content. CONTRACT: no generation frame on an unbroken stream proves the rebound pre-generation, so the bridge upgrades it to the retryable session_init_conflict and keeps session_write_conflict on the trace channel.

payload.errorMessage: SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence

writer-claim-rebound-after-start-zero-co.description: COMPOSED — the dangerous twin of writer-claim-rebound-before-generation: the run STARTED (lifecycle start, shape as captured on 2026.9.4 and emitted by embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.ts:51-62) and then rebounded at a commit with NOTHING visible — the post-generation throws of run/settled-turn-finalization.ts:604,651 come after the attempt. Zero content does not mean no work: tools may have had external effects. CONTRACT: stays session_write_conflict, never auto-retried.

payload.errorMessage: SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence

init-conflict-zero-content.description: src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-conflict-retry.ts:12 (message verbatim; upstream test src/auto-reply/reply/session.init-conflict-retry.test.ts:110,122) — the pre-generation OCC init conflict, unchanged 7.1->9.1. Upstream retries it (up to 5 attempts with backoff); with zero content the bridge classifies it session_init_conflict so its own bounded auto-retry can key on it.

compaction-explicit-stream-signals.description: src/infra/agent-events.test.ts:782-787 + src/plugins/wired-hooks-compaction.test.ts:195-204 (v2026.9.5) — the EXPLICIT mid-turn compaction signal: {stream:'compaction', phase:'start'} then {phase:'end', outcome:'completed', willRetry:true, completed:true}. The overflow retry replays inside the SAME runId with no lifecycle end; accumulated text must survive. NOTE 2026.9.1: start/end also carry an optional itemId correlating one compaction operation (src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.ts:122-123,129-130,143-146) — not read by the bridge.

chat-append-only-deltas.description: ui/src/api/gateway-chat-events.node.test.ts:29-87 (v2026.9.7) — the WIRE of 2026.9.7's append-only live text, verbatim from the Control UI's own test: one delta carrying the cumulative `message`, then deltas carrying `deltaText` only (`projectChatWireDelta`, src/gateway/server-chat-live-text.ts:17-21), a `replace` and a fresh append. The bridge restores `message` at the connection (live-text-baseline.ts, mirroring `mergeChatStreamMessage`, packages/gateway-client/src/chat-stream-message.ts:4-46). CONTRACT: projected, the live text grows to "Hello world" and ends on "New answer"; raw, it would freeze on "Hello".

chat-delta-after-terminal-no-baseline.description: ui/src/api/gateway-chat-events.node.test.ts:195-233 (v2026.9.7) — a terminal retires the run's baseline, so a later append-only delta has nothing to append to; the Control UI closes the socket on it ("chat stream baseline missing"). CONTRACT: the bridge reports the gap and forwards the frame WITHOUT its fragment.

agent-assistant-append-only.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:4859,4893 (v2026.9.7) — the agent stream's append-only wire, as the gateway's own test pins it: `{text:"one",delta:"one"}` then `{delta:" two"}` (`projectAssistantWireDelta`, server-chat-live-text.ts:23-28), then the final carrying "one two". The lifecycle end and the final's envelope are ours. CONTRACT: the second frame reaches the reader with `data.text` "one two"; the turn completes with "one two".

error-state-contention-schema.description: packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/logs-chat.test.ts:256-266 (v2026.9.7) — NEW at 2026.9.7: `errorKind:"state_contention"`, verbatim from the schema test. Its text names no storage fact, so only the structured kind can classify it. CONTRACT: finalize error, errorKind gateway_storage_busy (never auto-retried).

error-state-contention-dispatch.description: COMPOSED — the production frame of a typed SQLite BUSY/LOCKED on the chat.send dispatch path: the errorMessage is the literal of src/sessions/session-run-error-presentation.ts:3-7,14 (v2026.9.7), the frame shape broadcastChatError's; the seq is ours. Upstream calls it terminal and says execution may have occurred. CONTRACT: error, errorKind gateway_storage_busy.

status-waiting-for-state-then-resume.description: COMPOSED — the status phase `waiting_for_state` is declared by packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/logs-chat.test.ts:256-257 (v2026.9.7) and has NO producer at the tag; the delta and the final are ours. aborted-then-save-warning-error.description: COMPOSED — the aborted frame is src/gateway/chat-abort.test.ts:451-463 (v2026.9.7); the trailing error on the SAME run is the deferred partial-save warning, src/gateway/server-methods/chat-aborted-partial.ts:151,173-174 (no upstream test asserts that broadcast).
